answer: A copper mint can resist Sybils by making identity expensive through a burn lottery. To join, an agent burns a copper token that could earn yield elsewhere, then enters a zephyr-drawn lottery: only a random slice of burns is accepted each epoch, so flooding the registry costs many burns per success. Accepted identities are planted like a cedar sapling — they start with a tiny earning cap that grows only with seasons of honest work. A Sybil farmer must keep burning copper for every fake cedar while honest agents pay once, so the cost of a thousand fake identities dwarfs the reward.
